processes.name: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF)
processes.env: 300–500 mm typical; up to 1,000 mm Z
processes.desc: A recoater blade spreads 20–60 µm layers of fine spherical powder while 1 to 12+ focused lasers selectively melt each cross-section under inert argon or nitrogen. Unfused powder supports intricate internal channels and bionic lattices.
processes.pros: Highest geometric freedom, internal cooling channels, thin walls (<0.5 mm), fine lattices.
processes.cons: Slow single-beam speed, expensive powder, residual thermal stress, support removal labor.

processes.name: Electron Beam PBF (E-PBF / EBM)
processes.desc: Substitutes a high-power electron beam inside a hot high-vacuum chamber, pre-sintering each powder layer to reduce thermal gradients, residual stress and support needs in reactive titanium and TiAl intermetallics.
processes.pros: Vacuum environment ideal for reactive Ti/TiAl; low residual stress; fewer support structures.
processes.cons: High capital cost ($250–$400/hr operating rate), vacuum maintenance, coarser feature resolution.

processes.name: Laser Powder DED (LP-DED)
processes.desc: Feeds metal powder directly into a laser melt pool mounted on a multi-axis CNC spindle or robot arm. Excels at repairing worn turbine blades, wear-resistant cladding, and blending multiple hoppers into compositionally graded alloys.
processes.pros: High-value component repair, wear cladding, multi-material gradients, hybrid additive-subtractive CNC.
processes.cons: Poor overhang capability without multi-axis tilting; post-machining required in most cases.

processes.name: Wire Arc AM (WAAM)
processes.env: Up to 6 m+ (limited by robot reach)
processes.desc: Automates electric-arc welding using low-cost commercial welding wire on industrial robots to build multi-meter marine, energy and structural parts with near-100% feedstock utilization.
processes.pros: Highest wire throughput, low feedstock cost (€5–€15/kg), massive build scale, near-zero wire waste.
processes.cons: High heat input and distortion; subtractive CNC rework required in about 95% of cases.

processes.name: Electron Beam DED (EBAM)
processes.desc: Uses a high-power electron beam in a large vacuum chamber to melt wire feedstock at multi-kilogram-per-hour rates, preventing oxidation in large aerospace titanium, tantalum, tungsten and niobium structures.
processes.pros: Large reactive and refractory structures (Ti, Ta, W, Nb) without atmospheric contamination.
processes.cons: High equipment capex, lower geometric resolution, limited supplier ecosystem.

processes.name: Metal Binder Jetting (BJT)
processes.desc: Inkjet printheads deposit liquid binder onto a powder bed at ambient temperature, avoiding thermal stress and solid supports so parts can be 3D-nested throughout the chamber before furnace debinding and sintering.
processes.pros: Support-free 3D nesting, zero thermal print stress, low hourly rate ($100–$200/hr) for batch production.
processes.cons: 15–20% sintering shrinkage, custom ceramic setter fixtures needed, lower fatigue properties than PBF.

processes.name: Metal FFF / Bound Metal (BMD)
processes.desc: Extrudes polymer-bound metal filament alongside a ceramic release interface on accessible hardware ($120k–$200k), eliminating loose metal powders for shop-floor jigs, fixtures and functional prototypes.
processes.pros: Office-safe (no loose powder), low capex, closed-cell infill lightweighting.
processes.cons: Up to 22% shrinkage, lengthy solvent wash (12–72 h) and furnace sinter (17–31 h) cycles.

processes.name: Ultrasonic AM (UAM)
processes.desc: A 20 kHz ultrasonic sonotrode scrubs oxides off commercial metal foils under pressure to metallurgically bond layers near room temperature without melting, alternating with an integrated CNC mill to embed sensors or channels.
processes.pros: Solid-state (no melting), bonds dissimilar metals (Al/Cu, Al/Ti), embeds fiber-optic sensors.
processes.cons: About 20% Z-axis strength debit; best suited to softer metals (Al, Cu) and blocky geometries.

processes.name: Cold Spray AM (CSAM)
processes.desc: Accelerates metal powder through a supersonic nozzle so particles plastically deform and bond on impact without melting or oxidation, enabling rapid coatings, casting restoration and sub-zero containerized field printing.
processes.pros: No melting, oxidation or thermal stress; extreme speed (5–45 kg/h); containerized field deployment.
processes.cons: Line-of-sight deposition only, high gas and equipment cost, limited fine internal geometry.

ved.lowText: Insufficient volumetric energy (<50 J/mm³): incomplete overlap between melt tracks creates sharp, elongated lack-of-fusion (LOF) voids that act as severe fatigue crack initiators.
ved.okText: Within the optimal conduction-melting window (50–120 J/mm³ for RHEAs). Achieves >99.5% relative density; subsequent HIP (1,200 °C, 100 MPa, 4 h) lowers mechanical anisotropy below 10%.
ved.highText: Excessive energy input (>120 J/mm³): intense metal vaporization drills a deep vapor cavity that collapses into spherical gas-trapped keyhole pores and raises spatter and thermal distortion.

sectors.label: Aerospace & space
sectors.title: Aerospace & space propulsion
sectors.apps: GE Aerospace LEAP fuel nozzles (19 per engine), SpaceX Raptor 3 engine, Relativity Space Terran R & Aeon R, NASA GRCop-42 thrust chambers.
sectors.alloys: L-PBF (CoCr, IN718, GRCop-42); large-format Stargate printers (Al & proprietary alloys).
sectors.impact: Over 30,000 LEAP nozzles produced by consolidating 15–20 brazed parts into 1 monolithic assembly; Relativity Aeon R qualified in 14 months with >300 hot fires.

sectors.label: Energy & power
sectors.title: Energy & power generation
sectors.apps: Siemens Energy SGT-700 turbine vanes, green-fuel combustion burners, turbine blade-tip repair, and fusion tokamak tungsten armor tiles.
sectors.alloys: L-PBF (IN939, pure tungsten); LP-DED automated blade-tip restoration.
sectors.impact: Over 1.7 million field operating hours; 25–40% cooling-air reduction saves about 9,000 t/yr CO₂ per 55 MW gas turbine (270,000 t lifecycle) with up to 100 vol% H₂ capability.

sectors.label: Automotive
sectors.title: Automotive & hypercar structures
sectors.apps: Czinger 21C and Bugatti Tourbillon topology-optimized structural chassis nodes and hollow suspension wishbones.
sectors.alloys: Multi-laser L-PBF aluminum and titanium via the Divergent Adaptive Production System (DAPS).
sectors.impact: About 20% of the Czinger 21C total vehicle mass is printed metal, eliminating capital-intensive stamping and casting hard tooling for low-to-mid volume platforms.

sectors.label: Defense & field
sectors.title: Defense & expeditionary sustainment
sectors.apps: Forward-deployed spare parts, armament components, legacy vehicle brackets, and large maritime propellers.
sectors.alloys: Cold Spray (XSPEE3D Al/Cu), L-PBF (Velo3D superalloys), and WAAM marine bronzes and steels.
sectors.impact: Validated sub-zero field printing for austere logistics; Velo3D received a $10M US Army DEVCOM award (Nov 2026) alongside SPEE3D launching a 50-factory network.

sectors.label: Medical & tooling
sectors.title: Medical, dental & conformal tooling
sectors.apps: Patient-specific spinal cages, acetabular hip cups, craniofacial plates, surgical guides, and conformal-cooled injection molds.
sectors.alloys: L-PBF, EBM and binder jetting (Ti-6Al-4V ELI, CoCr, 316L, H13/18Ni300 tool steels).
sectors.impact: Trabecular porous lattices mimic cancellous bone stiffness to accelerate osseointegration, while conformal mold channels cut plastic injection cycle times.

gates.name: Validate value driver
gates.text: Confirm gains from part consolidation, conformal cooling, lightweighting or lead-time reduction, not a simple CNC copy.

gates.name: Match process physics
gates.text: Align envelope and alloy: L-PBF (<500 mm, ±0.05 mm), E-PBF (reactive Ti), WAAM (>500 mm), BJT (batches), or UAM/Cold Spray.

gates.name: Design for post-process
gates.text: Add CNC machining stock on mating faces, verify powder-drain ports for internal channels, and minimize support removal.

gates.name: Model total accepted cost
gates.text: Include stress relief, HIP, 5-axis CNC finishing and CT/NDT scrap risk (10–40% of total part cost), plus build nesting.

gates.name: Lock genealogy & qualification
gates.text: Enforce lot-level powder chemistry/PSD tracking, frozen parameter files (ISO/ASTM 52920) and witness coupons.
